Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36469: refactor: deduplicate block validation state catcher

c9cccf6d68c682e533876b4450f5ad7044a79f10 refactor: deduplicate block validation state catcher (Enoch Azariah)

Pull request description:

  As mentioned in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34644#discussion_r2889315162 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35675#discussion_r360301816, the validation state catchers were defined in the block template manager, `submitblock` rpc and mining test helpers, even though they do the same thing.

  Moved this helper into `node/block_validation_state_catcher.h` and reuse it across all three callers. An optional validation state replaces the separate `found` flag where used, preserving each caller's registration and result handling

  Replaces #36389 with the same commit on a dedicated branch.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36294: mempool: Remove -persistmempoolv1 option

731b89c09bbc286801eebf5061b161c3d5091150 test: Check that importmempool fails on a malformed mempool.dat (Fabian Jahr)
4c01625f798b4017ab83f86ab8815d56b4d18042 doc: Add release note for -persistmempoolv1 removal (Fabian Jahr)
d1dfdf827619bd06ff9c52e42f2c370e6e70504f mempool: Remove -persistmempoolv1 option (Fabian Jahr)
86a31b93d0db7f01e5c1a61fb014b89b2506fe54 test: Use v31.0 as old node in mempool_compatibility.py (Fabian Jahr)

Pull request description:

  `-persistmempoolv1` was added in #28207 as a temporary option to allow downgrading to v26 and earlier, which can't read the XOR'ed `mempool.dat`. v26 has now been EOL for a while. So any version this option could help downgrade to is unsupported now. It seems ready for removal. I don't think this requires an additional deprecation cycle since the feature is useless for any maintained version and docs have always stated that this was a "temporary option that will be removed in the future".

  Reading v1 files is still supported, so upgrading directly from an old version keeps the persisted mempool.

  `mempool_compatibility.py` now uses v28.2 as the old node, the oldest release in `get_previous_releases.py` that writes the current format.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36440: test: speed up functional tests by removing avoidable waits

8dc80cafa2ee5932c9ff499c02d6ab8e3cf2f5ef test: wake p2p wait_until on message delivery instead of polling (ViniciusCestarii)
10cfeb33357c937ddd9f588a35e0f8f33abd6ece test: set noban_tx_relay to speed up slow tx relay tests (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Reduce functional test runtime:

  - set noban_tx_relay = True for tests that can benefit from it.
  - wake P2PInterface.wait_until as soon as a message is delivered or the connection state changes, instead of polling every 50ms.

  Tested on my x86-64 machine:

  Wall time (-j=18): 110.8s to 99.1s (-11%)
  Accumulated: 1715s to 1411s (-17.5%)

  Tests that were most affected:

  | test | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | feature_maxuploadtarget | 57.9s | 6.2s |
  | wallet_conflicts | 49.2s | 7.0s |
  | p2p_sendheaders | 31.1s | 6.8s |
  | p2p_compactblocks | 11.1s | 1.7s |
  | wallet_orphanedreward | 9.3s | 5.2s |
  | wallet_importprunedfunds | 4.9s | 2.9s |

ci: refactor BUILD_TARGETS use

"all" is added to the build targets unless GOAL is "all" or contains
"codegen". This implicit translation can be confusing, so explicitly
spell out the targets as "all", "all deploy", etc., where needed.

Also, use the eval-based string-to-argv conversion for BUILD_TARGETS to
avoid disabling shellcheck SC2086.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35989: wallet: fix crash on importdescriptors with a range ending at 2^31-1

93c8aec3fbc8c5a2fcc834c4acc1b7d96bffa9a0 doc: add release note for #35989 (Shuvam Pandey)
457c9e8999fbee1d37f41eaede681f787e657395 script: avoid overflow when checking descriptor range bounds (Shuvam Pandey)
ab3bb55a67cced3551e8ebb658c4d962a10d3715 test: add coverage for descriptor range end bounds (Shuvam Pandey)
867ad9bffbd3ab26c9899207ddd11380e0c1a1bd wallet: fix integer overflow in descriptor keypool top up (Shuvam Pandey)
1889440f821d6bf8394050c96cc8e06a2f18d9c2 wallet: reject unrepresentable descriptor import ranges (Shuvam Pandey)

Pull request description:

  `WalletDescriptor` stores an exclusive range end in `int32_t`. Importing
  `[2147483647, 2147483647]` produces an end of `2^31`, which narrows to a negative
  value and aborts the node during keypool top-up. An import without a range can
  hit the same issue with an oversized `-keypool`.

  Check the exclusive end before constructing the wallet descriptor, covering
  both explicit and default ranges. The bound stays wallet-specific: scanning
  RPCs still accept `INT32_MAX` as an inclusive endpoint.

  Also calculate the keypool top-up endpoint in `int64_t` before checking its
  bound, and reject reversed ranges before computing `high - low` in
  `CheckDescriptorRangeBounds`. These fix the overflows reached by
  `keypoolrefill INT32_MAX` after advancing a descriptor, and by `[INT64_MAX, 0]`,
  respectively. Regression tests cover all three fixes.

  I tested on macOS arm64 with Clang 22 and UBSan passed: 34 targeted unit
  cases and the importdescriptors, keypool, deriveaddresses (RPC and CLI),
  scantxoutset, and scanblocks functional tests.
